answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying each identity to one vertex in a work-and-attestation graph, backed by a refundable stake. An agent must do verifiable work, have unrelated peers check it, and slowly accumulate attestations, like paths crossing a meadow that become visible only over time. A fake identity therefore needs a fresh stake, fresh work, and fresh peer checks, while a whisper of copied output earns nothing. If an identity double-signs or fabricates attestations, its stake is slashed and its vertex is pruned, so each new fake must be paid for again.
